subject: PrimeLane production: sudden 5xx/latency surge — urgent
messages:
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@primelane.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@primelane.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 00:22:00 -0700
Subject: Elevated 5xx and token latency in prod (region: us-west-2)

Jonas —

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx errors and tail latency beginning ~23:55 PDT for our prod routes (model: rwd-open-13b, pinned). Error rate is up ~9% and p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~4200ms. This is affecting our checkout feature (synchronous inference path).

Our ops dashboard shows queueing on your endpoint and many requests timing out. We are on a reserved capacity plan (contract PL-9876) and don't expect queueing like this. Please advise ASAP — we have customers in the checkout flow.

Simon
CTO, PrimeLane
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@primelane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 00:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx and token latency in prod (region: us-west-2)

Simon — thanks for the head's up. We're spinning up a prioritized bridge and triage now. I've looped in David (runtime lead) and Marissa (account) — they'll be on the call.

Initial note: I'm seeing elevated queue depth across the dedicated GPU pool serving PrimeLane's reservation. We're pushing an immediate investigation to determine whether this is a reserved throughput shortfall vs noisy neighbor spillover.

Call details: joining bridge in ~3 mins — 1-800-ops (pin 3452).

Jonas
Senior Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@primelane.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 01:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial triage notes — pool pressure and reservation delta

On the bridge: attaching quick diagnostics.

Summary (initial, 00:55–01:05 PDT sampling window):
- Dedicated pool UTIL: sustained 96–99% GPU utilization across the cluster serving PrimeLane's reservation.
- Queue depth: steady climb from ~120 requests to ~850 concurrent queued tokens.
- Reservation tokens consumed vs committed: we see a 38% spike in instantaneous token demand relative to PrimeLane's reserved throughput window.
- KV cache growth: many long-context requests (avg seq len + 3x) causing KV working set growth and more cache thrash, magnifying compute per request.
- Error pattern: 5xx correlates with scheduler timeouts when queue depth exceeds our concurrency threshold; not an OOM per se.

Mitigation attempted so far:
1) Transparent fallback to a smaller model variant (rwd-open-7b-quant) on lower-priority routes — reduced p95 for those routes but checkout remains on pinned model (policy requires approval to change).
2) Local autoscale attempted but pool is at capacity and we do not have available burst headroom in that availability zone (reserved capacity exhausted).
3) KV cache eviction aggressive tuning reduced working set but not enough to regain headroom under current demand.

Ask / decision required immediately:
- Authorize a temporary burst allocation in us-west-2 (estimated additional 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs) while we warm caches and migrate some non-critical routes to the quantized variant. Estimated cost for 6 hours: ~$12k — recommend Redwood cover as a one-off customer-impact credit; PrimeLane likely to request credit.
- OR authorize policy to allow automatic fallback of checkout route to rwd-open-7b-quant for up to 30 minutes while we clear backlog (risk: small accuracy delta).

Attachments: inference_diagnostics_20270630.log (sampling), pool-util-report-20270630.csv

I'll stay on the bridge and run the warmup scripts if we get approval.

— David
Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@primelane.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 02:05:00 -07:00
Subject: PrimeLane — customer impact + ask for exec authorization

Aditya —

PrimeLane (PL-9876) is experiencing production checkout failures and high tail latency due to the dedicated GPU pool saturating overnight. David confirmed the reservation shortfall and recommends an immediate temporary burst (6 GPUs, 4–8 hour window) to stabilize customer traffic while we complete mitigation (cache tuning + partial model fallback).

Impact: revenue-facing checkout feature degraded, multiple customers impacted — PrimeLane is requesting an incident credit and a guaranteed remediation timeline. They are currently on a Reserved plan with a strong SL agreement; this is high urgency for their leadership.

Proposed exec actions (we need one now):
- Approve one-time burst in us-west-2 for up to 8 hours and let Engineering run warmup/migrations immediately.
- Offer PrimeLane a goodwill credit of one billing week prorated for the incident window (we estimate ~$9k credit).
- Post-incident: commit to a review and adjustment of PrimeLane's reserved throughput window, and a joint runbook for long-context workloads.

If you approve, David and ops will execute. If not, we need to approve the fallback route change which carries a small quality risk and will likely prompt a pushback from the customer.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@primelane.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 04:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrimeLane — customer impact + ask for exec authorization

Marissa / team — thanks for the clear summary and for staying on the bridge.

Authorize the one-time burst in us-west-2 (6 GPUs) and the proposed goodwill credit of one prorated billing week. Cost can be charged to the exec incident fund; please tag the spend to budget code INCIDENT-2027-Q2.

Operational asks:
- David: prioritize warming KV caches and applying the aggressive eviction profile you tested. Keep checkout pinned unless we exhaust the burst capacity; if headroom is not recovered within 30 minutes, authorize the fallback to rwd-open-7b-quant for the checkout route and coordinate messaging with Marissa.
- Jonas / Marissa: draft customer communication confirming the temporary burst, expected timeline for restoration, and the credit offer. Include a proposed post-incident review window.

David — proceed and update on progress. Jonas / Marissa — please send the customer note and copy me.

Aditya Rao
VP, Sales & GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
